questions: Should the server's current time appended to received data be the time at which the data was received, or the time when the response is sent?
What timestamp format should be used? (e.g., ISO 8601, custom format like 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS')
If a client sends multiple messages before receiving a response, should each be queued and responded to individually, or only the latest?
Should the server handle partial recv (data less than buffer_size) as a complete message, or wait for more?
If a socket becomes writable but its queue is empty, should it be removed from outputs immediately or after a timeout?
Should the server close sockets on any exception (e.g., send error), or only on empty recv?
Is the run_duration inclusive of the time spent in the finally block closing the server, or only the select loop?
Should the server's status message include the actual elapsed time or just the run_duration parameter?
